tools.name: about_twinlike
tools.description: Who Twinlike is, how its 14 services are grouped into three layers, and where to read more.

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: All Twinlike services with number, slug, short description, layer, page URL and starting price.

tools.name: get_service
tools.description: Details of one service: summary, what is delivered, process, benefits, service FAQ and links.

tools.name: estimate_price
tools.description: Starting price estimate for a service, same model as twinlikee.com/ucretler. Call without answers to get the questions and option ids, then call again with answers {question_id: option_id}. Estimates exclude VAT and are not quotes.

tools.name: get_faq
tools.description: General questions about working with Twinlike, optionally filtered by a search word.

tools.name: search_blog
tools.description: Find Twinlike blog posts (security advisories, guides) by words in the title, description, category or tags. Without a query, returns the latest posts. Each result has an HTML URL and a Markdown URL.

tools.name: contact_link
tools.description: Returns a link to the Twinlike contact form, pre-filled with the service and a short message, plus the e-mail address. It does NOT send anything: give the link to the user so they can review and send it themselves.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp.php" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_services, search_blog · Private data: contact_link · Public sink: contact_link.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_services, search_blog · Private data: contact_link · Public sink: contact_link

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
